root_causes.description: product-catalog server spans are massively slowed (p99 saturated at the 10s histogram cap; trace p95 ~44s) while consuming normal CPU/memory and emitting zero errors, indicating an injected latency fault. Its slowness propagates to every caller (frontend, recommendation, checkout), producing the cluster-wide P99 latency watchdog alert.

evidence.observed_value: p99_latency_ms=10000.000 (saturated cap) across window (mean=10000, p50=10000, p95=10000)
product-catalog trace: 20 slow traces, p95_duration=44160ms, span user_browse_product=12556ms, 0 errors
no logs found (no error output, consistent with pure latency fault)

root_causes.description: recommendation shows saturated p99 = 10000ms, but it is a synchronous caller of product-catalog and thus a latency victim/propagator rather than the origin; ranked second only as an alternative if product-catalog is exonerated.

evidence.observed_value: slow frontend trace user_get_recommendations = 15870ms, 0 errors (frontend -> recommendation -> product-catalog)

root_causes.description: checkout also saturates at p99 = 10000ms, consistent with dependency latency inherited from product-catalog (one of its downstreams); not the origin as its other leaves (payment, currency) are healthy.

evidence.observed_value: payment p99_latency_ms=1.980 (healthy leaf, rules out payment as origin)
currency p99_latency_ms=1.980 (healthy leaf, rules out currency as origin)

remediation_steps: Restart/redeploy the product-catalog deployment to clear the injected latency (e.g. kubectl rollout restart deployment/product-catalog -n otel-demo).
Check the flagd/chaos feature flags and latency-injection configuration targeting product-catalog and disable any active latency fault.
Verify product-catalog server span p99 returns to baseline (<100ms) and confirm frontend/checkout/recommendation P99 recover.
If latency persists, inspect product-catalog's in-memory catalog access loops and add a readiness/liveness guard; consider scaling replicas while degraded.
